title: Barbara George's hit, Juggy Murray and AFO's pride
summary: AFO had hits with Prince La La and Barbara George until Murray bought her contract and froze their releases; Tyler still counts AFO a success.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So, we put out a couple of records. The first one was put the hit on me with Prince Lala.
Right.
And then, I know with Barbara George, that took off.
Right.
Now, Juggy Murray, the guy who had put up the money, got so greedy when he got this number two record in the nation, uh, whatever, that he got greedy. He wanted her contract.
Right.
And he insisted he had to have a contract. So, he offered us $25,000 for our contract, which was pretty good back then.
Back then, yeah.
But he didn't really have to do this. We owned her contract as a production company. He owned us.
Right.
And he already owned her.
Mm-hmm.
He didn't have to buy it.
Yeah.
So, he took her to New York, and they had no idea how to record her or what to do.
Yeah. Yeah.

And so, he, she never made anything after that. Right. And when he, the word got around that he was rather stupid in doing what he did, he froze all, all, uh, he wouldn't release any of our records anymore.
Mm-hmm.
So, we were left without an outlet. So, we tried to do it on ourselves, by ourselves, and we just never could do it.
So, do you, do you see that AFO is a failure in any way?
Oh, no. Mm-hmm. I was very successful.
Mm-hmm. In what ways?
That we were the first, even before Motown, that came out with a, with a, a, a hit record by a black production company.
We, when you all got together, was that something, were you all proud that, that, hey, we're the, we're the first, I mean, we're the first guy.

Well, the thing is, we knew, we knew what we had done. Mm-hmm. And we were rather proud of it. And, uh, we had Cannonball Adley to come down and hang with us and actually did some jazz things that we, uh, you know, uh, uh, recorded. Mm-hmm. He sent down a couple of people we, he wanted us to record and things like that. And, uh, he, uh, would come down and other people would come, come in too. And we did some good things, but we just didn't have the, the, uh, outlet to, to, you know, like Willie T, Eddie Bull. Right. Uh, people like that. And we just didn't have any outlet to, you know, we didn't have the, the clout to, to do anything with it.
